mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 4.5% in a monthly reading, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 45% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or Rank IC falls below 0.01 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both housing starts and retail sales indicates a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or Rank IC is below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO below 100), manufacturing sector weakness reduces corporate profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average indicates strong consumer spending, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average, or Rank IC is below 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0%, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy stance that increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or Rank IC is below 0.01 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in unemployment rate and decline in non-farm payrolls signals a deteriorating labor market, which reduces consumer confidence and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls, or Rank IC is below 0.02 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI index exceeds 270, it indicates a high inflation environment that typically leads to restrictive monetary policy, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 270, or Rank IC is below 0.02 over 3-year windows.
